model: Underlying profit capitalisation at cost of equity, prime-property AFFO-equivalent stream plus build-to-sell wind-down in the equity bridge (engine route)

inputs.share_count_basis: 2,133.3m shares in issue at 30 June 2026 (H1 FY2026 interim) plus 6.4m dilutive awards (diluted weighted 2,152.2m less basic weighted 2,145.8m, interim note 8). Held FLAT: buybacks (US$650m programme, US$157.3m spent H1 FY2026, US$301.4m FY2025) are funded from recycled build-to-sell capital, which is already credited in the equity bridge; shrinking the count as well would count the same capital twice.
inputs.net_debt_treatment: Held at ZERO. The stream is underlying profit attributable to shareholders, which is already after net financing charges on the US$3.4bn net debt (and after the interest earned on the US$2.67bn cash). Subtracting net debt again would deduct the debt twice.
inputs.reported_fcf_basis: FY2025 underlying profit attributable to shareholders (revised basis, prime properties investment only) US$458.2m less maintenance capex at 12% of the stream (FY2025 maintenance capex US$63m, FY2024 US$53m, AR FY2025 adjusted-FCF reconciliation). Statutory OCF less major renovations was US$420.2m; company adjusted FCF US$810m includes US$291m of build-to-sell JV cash, which is valued in the bridge instead.
inputs.sbc_source: Share-based payment expense US$7.3m FY2025 (CSV StockBasedComp) is already expensed inside underlying profit, so it is charged once there; sbc_incl_equity_taxes and the SBC path are 0 to avoid a second deduction. Effectively an SBC-zero case: house and street coincide.
inputs.interest_income_note: Interest received (US$39.9m FY2025, US$36.3m H1 FY2026) sits inside net financing charges in underlying profit and the cash is not added back, so nothing to strip.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 repurchase of shares in financing activities US$301.4m; H1 FY2026 US$157.3m (~21m shares). A real repurchaser, funded by capital recycling.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Cost of equity 8.5% in USD (HKD is pegged to USD, flows reported in USD): US 10-year risk-free ~4.25% + beta ~0.85 x 5.0% ERP. Applied as a cost of EQUITY because the stream is post-interest. Not varied by scenario (risk charged once, through the weights). For reference Wharf (0004.HK) was capitalised at 9.5% HKD CoE with heavier mainland exposure; HKL is 74% HK Central and 11% geared.
inputs.lease_treatment: Immaterial (lease liabilities US$2.9m FY2025); lease cost is inside underlying profit. No separate lease line.
inputs.nci_treatment: Stream is attributable to shareholders (NCI US$39.5m of equity, profit share ~US$3m); charged once by using the attributable figure. No NCI bridge deduction.
inputs.notes: MODEL CHOICE: routed by .claude/skills/dcf-methods/SKILL.md. Hongkong Land is not a REIT, but its value is an IAS 40 fair-value investment-property portfolio, so it belongs to the REIT/property row, not the owner-FCF row: statutory net income is dominated by revaluation swings (+US$4.7bn FY2017, -US$3.4bn FY2020, +US$0.7bn H1 FY2026) and owner-FCF/EBITDA/net debt do not mean what the engine assumes. It straddles two rows, so the parts are valued separately and summed: (1) the prime properties investment business by capitalising underlying profit (the company's own audited earnings measure, post-interest and post-tax, which since FY2025 excludes build-to-sell) less maintenance capex, at the cost of equity with net debt held at zero, same family as 0004.HK Wharf UNP-at-CoE; (2) the build-to-sell wind-down, reclassified to non-trading in FY2025, at a haircut to book in the equity bridge, less the outstanding capital commitments that fund the growth path's new openings. NAV/share (US$14.71 at 30 June 2026) is reported as a cross-check, not the model, because it capitalises rents at the private-market 2.9-3.5% cap rates of the independent valuers, a rate no 15%-hurdle buyer of the listed equity earns. ENGINE MAPPING: revenue = underlying profit stream; EBITDA margin 100%; SBC, D&A, tax, working capital 0 (all already inside the post-tax stream); capex = maintenance capex as % of stream. Year 1 is FY2026 and is discounted a full year from the October 2026 valuation date (engine end-of-year convention), mildly conservative. No prior DCF existed: fresh build.

equity_bridge.item: Build-to-sell properties for sale at 75% of book
equity_bridge.note: Properties for sale US$942.5m at 30 June 2026 (interim balance sheet). 25% haircut for mainland China residential price risk (US$372m post-tax provision taken FY2025) and a 3-4 year realisation lag at the cost of equity.

equity_bridge.item: Build-to-sell associates and JVs at 75% of book
equity_bridge.note: Non-strategic (build-to-sell) associates and JVs US$2,525.2m at 30 June 2026 (interim note 11). Same 25% haircut. Equity-accounted, so already net of JV-level debt.

equity_bridge.item: Assets held for sale at book
equity_bridge.note: Interim note 12: remaining One Exchange Square floors contracted to HKEX at US$158.8m plus US$50.5m JV interest. Contracted cash; the small rental income those floors still earn is in the FY2025 base and is absorbed by the growth path.

Interim note 15, 30 June 2026 (incl. Bangkok JV contributions and Tomorrow's CENTRAL). The growth path credits the income from these projects, so their remaining cost is charged here; it is not in the post-interest stream.

historical_growth.eps_basis: Underlying EPS (statutory EPS is negative in FY2020-FY2024 on revaluation losses, so a statutory CAGR is undefined). FY2025 is on the revised basis ex build-to-sell; earlier years include it, so the CAGR overstates the decline of the prime business (FY2024 restated 22.60c -> FY2025 20.98c is -7%).
historical_growth.fcf_basis: Statutory OCF less major renovations; FY2020 was -US$3.6bn (Westbund land acquisition) so the 5-year CAGR is undefined.
historical_growth.growth_rate_source: Forward judgment, not a historical CAGR: every trailing series is negative after six years of falling Hong Kong Central office rents and the build-to-sell exit. 5.5% is the approximate 10-year CAGR of the base-case underlying profit path (FY2026 guided ~+11%, decelerating to 3%).
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (-2.6%/-2.9%) diverges by more than 30% from revenue (-13.6%) and underlying EPS (-15.2%) CAGRs. Revenue is distorted by build-to-sell sales and its FY2025 reclassification; equity by revaluations. Neither is a usable forward growth anchor.
historical_growth.notes: No SBC adjustment distorts the FCF series (SBC is US$1-7m/yr, inside underlying profit). The history is a down-cycle: HK Central office average rent fell from HK$110+ psf (2019) to HK$91 psf (H1 FY2026), and underlying profit fell from US$1,076m (FY2019, incl. build-to-sell) to US$458m (FY2025, prime only).

base.growth_rates_rationale: FY2026 +11% is management's upgraded guidance (H1 underlying +11%, full year 'broadly in line'), driven mainly by lower net financing charges from recycling already done. FY2027-29 +9/8/7%: HK Central office rents stabilise in 2027 and grow from 2028 (rents +11% off the Q3 2025 trough, Core Central vacancy 9.2%), LANDMARK reopens fully from Tomorrow's CENTRAL (40% of space under renovation in H1 FY2026), Westbund Phase 2 leases up and Phase 3 opens from 2028, Suzhou/Chongqing open 2027, >=US$25m cost saves from 2027 (~5% of the stream) and SCPREF fees grow, offset by income lost on assets sold (MBFC T3, One Exchange Square floors, Singapore into SCPREF). Fades to 3% by FY2035, leaving underlying profit ~US$826m, still below the FY2019 level. Future build-to-sell recycling's interest saving is NOT in this path (that capital is in the bridge).
base.capex_rationale: Maintenance capex ~12% of the stream (US$63m on US$458m FY2025; US$53m on US$409m FY2024). Growth capex is charged through the commitments line in the bridge.
base.narrative: Hong Kong Central office recovers slowly, LANDMARK and Westbund deliver as planned, the pivot to recurring income works but no faster than guided.

bull.narrative: IPO-led demand absorbs the Central office overhang quickly and rents re-rate toward the 2019 level by 2030; Tomorrow's CENTRAL makes LANDMARK the region's top luxury address with double-digit reversions; Westbund Phase 3 and the CENTRAL-series malls stabilise on schedule; third-party AUM scales toward the US$100bn 2035 target so fees become a meaningful second stream. Underlying profit reaches ~US$970m by FY2035.

bear.narrative: The consultants' 7-15 year Hong Kong office absorption view proves right: the 2026 rebound fades, negative reversions return as new supply (including HKL's own One Causeway Bay) lands, mainland China retail stays mixed, and recycling sells income faster than redeployment replaces it. FY2026 still misses the +11% guide slightly (+8%), then the stream grows ~1-2% a year; heavier capex to keep the estate competitive.

scenario_narratives.base: Hong Kong Central office rents, which bottomed in Q3 2025, stabilise in 2027 and grow modestly from 2028; LANDMARK's Tomorrow's CENTRAL programme completes on schedule with positive reversions; Westbund Central Phases 2-3 and the Suzhou/Chongqing malls lease up; cost saves and fund fees add a few percent. Underlying profit compounds ~5.5% a year to ~US$826m by FY2035. The build-to-sell book is realised at ~75% of carrying value over 3-4 years and pays for the committed pipeline.
scenario_narratives.bull: A genuine Central office upcycle on the Hong Kong IPO pipeline and limited new supply, LANDMARK established as Asia's ultra-luxury flagship, the third-party capital platform scaling toward the 2035 AUM target, and the mainland commercial assets stabilising. Underlying profit roughly doubles by FY2035.
scenario_narratives.bear: Structural office oversupply in Hong Kong reasserts itself after the 2026 bounce, the mainland stays weak, and capital recycling sells income without equal redeployment. Underlying profit drifts ~1-2% a year after FY2026; the business is a low-growth 1.6%-ROE landlord whose value rests on its asset base rather than its earnings.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 20% (above the 15% default): the stream is 74% one submarket (Central office) with six years of falling rents behind it and the recovery rests on an unproven pivot to recurring income and fund management. Base 50%: guidance has just been upgraded and H1 FY2026 showed rents, vacancy and LANDMARK sales all moving the right way. Bull 30% (below the 35% default): it needs the office upcycle, the luxury retail re-rating and fund scaling to all happen together.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Hongkong Land is valued as what a minority holder of the listed equity actually receives: the recurring post-interest earnings of the prime portfolio, capitalised at a USD cost of equity, plus the cash still to come out of the build-to-sell wind-down. On that basis the stock is not cheap. The 44% discount to NAV (US$8.20 against US$14.71) is the market applying an equity return to assets the valuers mark at 2.9-3.5% private-market cap rates; an 8.5% cost of equity on a 1.6% ROE stream only reaches NAV if the assets are sold. The NAV case is real but it is a different trade: it pays off only through disposals at book (MBFC T3, the HKEX floors and the SCPREF seeding at NAV show HKL can do this) or a take-private by Jardine Matheson (~54% owner). Neither is a live corporate action, so neither is modelled. The buyback at 0.56x NAV adds to NAV per share, but on the earnings basis it is roughly value-neutral, because the 2.9% earnings yield bought back is about the yield given up by selling assets.

nav_cross_check.note: Underlying profit FY2026E ~US$508m on shareholders' funds US$31.4bn. Investment property valuation US$34.7bn attributable at FY2025 (HK office cap rates 2.90-3.50%, HK retail 4.25-5.00%).

key_risks_to_valuation: Cost of equity: terminal value is 59% of base value. A 1pp lower CoE (7.5%) lifts base value about 11% to US$5.75, and even at 6.5% the 20x terminal cap binds at US$6.41, still below the price. The market price cannot be reached on the earnings stream at any plausible equity rate; it is paying for NAV realisation.
NAV realisation: if HKL keeps selling or fund-seeding assets at valuation and buys back stock below NAV, realised value per share can run well above this earnings-based figure.
A Jardine Matheson take-private at a NAV-referenced price would make this model irrelevant.
The build-to-sell haircut (25%) is a judgment on mainland China residential pricing; each 10pp is ~US$0.16/share.
Hong Kong Central office oversupply: new supply including HKL's own One Causeway Bay could reverse the 2026 rent recovery.
Interest rates: 41% of debt is floating; higher HIBOR/SORA lifts net financing charges in the post-interest stream directly.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API (H78.SI, SGX, USD) at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 5.92-9.12.
